items.title: 15M web servers on one VM – smoltcp, DPDK, AF_XDP
items.summary: Article URL: https://kapteko.com/15-million-webservers/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50556533 Points: 297 # Comments: 32
items.content: Put a web server online and everyone starts trying to hack it. Why? A basic rule of economics. Short supply, big demand - there aren’t enough web servers for everyone. Let’s run a web server for every human on the planet, all 8 billion of them. I couldn’t get funding, so we’re bootstrapping. The goal is to run 15 million web servers on one VM with 10GB of RAM and 1 CPU core. If we succeed, I’ll find some RAM from old microwaves around the house and we’ll scale it up so everyone can have their own web server. Demand will drop to zero and cybersecurity will be solved once and for all. Web server Instead of vibe coding it all, let’s use an ancient technique called learning . First of all, what is a web server? There are a few essential syscalls. listen - syscall, asks kernel to listen for connections on a socket accept - syscall, accepts a connection on a socket recv - receives data from a socket send - sends data close - closes What is a syscall? A function that is executed by the OS kernel. Whatever fancy language or library you use for HTTP, it all comes down to those syscalls (well, yes, but actually no). Let’s use C to make it all explicit. We start listening, then read from the socket in a loop and always reply with OK . int main ( void ) { // We use port 0 which makes OS return any available port int server = socket ( AF_INET , SOCK_STREAM , 0 ); if ( listen ( server , 128 ) 0 ) return 1 ; const char reply [] = "HTTP/1.0 200 OK Content-Length: 2 OK" ; for ( int client ; ( client = accept ( server , NULL , NULL )) >= 0 ;) { if ( recv ( client , NULL , 4096 , MSG_TRUNC ) > 0 ) send ( client , reply , sizeof reply - 1 , MSG_NOSIGNAL ); close ( client ); } } It couldn’t be simpler: listen on a socket, accept a connection, read the data, send a reply, close the client connection, and repeat. It gives us around 65k RPS. Now that we’ve learned everything, let’s finish the article and call it a day: $ for i in $( seq 1 15_000_000 ); do echo $i ; ./server &; done ... ... 28232 program exited with error 1 Hm, why did listen fail? Ah, we’ve run out of ports! We’re using port=0 , so the kernel picks an available port from ip_local_port_range . $ sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 32768 60999 Why are so many ports skipped? Historically, port 0 was created for outbound connections. When you call connect('example.com', 80) , Linux connects to the remote server (the sending part) and then allocates a random port on the host from ip_local_port_range to receive data (the receiving part). There are a few reasons the default range is small. Port 0 is special. You cannot listen on it (actually, you can - https://acid.vegas/blog/the-port-that-does-not-exist/ ). Ports 1-1024 require root. Ports 1024-32768 are skipped to keep dynamically allocated ports from conflicting with existing apps. You don’t want to call connect('example.com') and end up allocating port 3306 to receive incoming data. mysql cannot start because you have example.com open in your Firefox would make for a confusing UX. Ports 60999 - 65535 are excluded for historical reasons dating back to IP Masquerading. Nothing prevents us from overriding the range and using 1-65535 , but that’s still a bit short of 15 million. A UDP server and a TCP server can use the same port, so we can double that to 128k. We could run a proxy in front to forward requests to the right process (virtual hosting, yay), but these are all ancient techniques - in the AI era, whenever you have a software problem, you just throw money at the hardware. Let’s simply connect 15M/32k=450 new network cards to the server. The 65k limit comes from the TCP standard. A port is a u16 , so even if we hack the kernel with find '*.c' -exec sed -i 's/u16/u32/' \; to support bigger port numbers, normal clients still wouldn’t be able to connect. Each listening server is identified by a (protocol, IP, port) tuple. That explains how we can use the same port for UDP and TCP. It also means we can use a bunch of different IPs for our web servers. If we connect 450 network cards to the server, we’ll get 450 unique IP addresses and be able to listen on 15 million unique addresses! UPD. I’ve heard from readers that the network card is the ONLY hardware component that didn’t get 100 times more expensive in the last year. Can’t we avoid ruining that too and solve this in software? Let’s use a beautiful technology called AnyIP , which lets us listen on a whole subnet. Many VPS and dedicated server providers routinely give you a whole TCPv6 subnet. We can simply run sudo ip -6 route add local 2001:db8:1234:5678::/64 dev lo to get 18 quintillion addresses (plus or minus one) to listen on. You can do the same for IPv4 - acquiring a subnet with 15M addresses would cost around $250 million, so adjust the command for your environment. We’ll change our server to pick the nth IP from our range: // Read IP index from CLI, shift base IP by it int i = read_cli_param ( argv [ 1 ]); const uint32_t base_ip = 0x 0a400001 ; // ex. 10.64.0.1 addr.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl ( first_ip + i ); // shift, ex. 10.64.0.2 And now we can finally finish the article. $ for i in $( seq 1 15_000_000 ); do echo $i ; ./server $i &; done ... ... Out of memory Hm, one server consumes 1.5MB of RAM, so running that many would take… 20TB of RAM, which is a few bytes more than our 10GB budget. Runtime By pure coincidence (what are the odds?), I explained in Running 10 million Codex CLIs on one server - LFI processes why running millions of processes creates too much overhead. The answer is to run them all in one process inside a custom runtime, much as V8 can run millions of guests in a single process. In Userland Linux scheduler in Rust , I showed how to build a specialised userland scheduler and switch between tasks with the absolute minimum amount of RAM per task. TLDR: We’re using LFI for sandboxing. It gives us memory isolation and replaces all syscalls with calls to our host handler, which lets us implement I/O however we like. To schedule multiple guests, we load them all into our main process’s memory and make the CPU constantly switch between guests - we become our own micro OS. Since we need to save every byte and CPU cycle we can, we’re doomed to build another specialised runtime. Let’s get started. How much is 10GB divided by 15M, exactly? Ten Great Britains divided by 15 million gives around half of kilo britain. Not much. If we run all our guests in our runtime, our custom scheduler needs to switch between them. What’s the absolute minimum state we need to preserve for each guest? We can ignore server initialisation and assume switches only happen within the main loop. Let’s take another look at the loop. for ( int client ; ( client = accept ( server , NULL , NULL )) >= 0 ;) { if ( recv ( client , NULL , 4096 , MSG_TRUNC ) > 0 ) send ( client , reply , sizeof reply - 1 , MSG_NOSIGNAL ); close ( client ); } This code has only two state variables, server and client . Both are simple file descriptors. If our scheduler had to suspend a guest at any syscall point in this loop, we’d need to save the following state: struct Context { pc : u64 , // Instruction address to return to fd_server : i32 , // server file descriptor fd_client : i32 , // client file descriptor } We only need 16 bytes per guest, so to run 15M guests in our runtime and be able to suspend them and switch between them, we would need 220MB of RAM. We’re playing it safe here - we don’t need the full u64 or i32 , and with bit packing, we could probably get down to 8 bytes per guest. What else do we need? $ codex "How much TCP connection takes?" Idle connection takes zero, while active connection consumes around 5kb Here’s what we get if we assume that only 1M of connections are active at any given moment. 14M idle connections - 0 bytes Scheduling state for 15M guests - 220MB 1M active connections at 5kb each = 5GB Only half of our RAM budget, yay! I don’t often exceed my own expectations. Let’s validate it: int main ( void ) { // Run 14M of idle connections - just listen and do nothing // SHOULD CONSUMER ZERO MEMORY! for ( int i = 0 ; i 14_000_000 ; i ++ ) { int server = socket ( AF_INET , SOCK_STREAM , 0 ); listen ( server , 1 ) } } $ ./run_15m_idle_servers Out Of Memory $ dmesg | tail -n 1 'SHOULD CONSUMER ZERO MEMORY' - what are you, stupid? Looks like the kernel still has some leftover comments from Linus. I’m not stupid, but I have to admit I was below average here. While an LLM is a significant boost for learning, it’s too easy to accept its answers without thinking critically and feel ashamed later on. But hey, embarrassment is a cost of entry - let’s dive into networking in the kernel. Networking in the kernel Remember when I said that our simple server uses only 5 syscalls? I missed one that was right in front of me. Let me highlight it: int main ( void ) { for ( int i = 0 ; i 10_000_000 ; ++ i ) { socket ( AF_INET , SOCK_STREAM , 0 ); } } That code will OOM in a 10GB VM. The socket syscall allocates around 3300 bytes, whether the socket is active, listening, or doing nothing. Linux was clearly written at a time when RAM was big and cheap, sigh. Let’s ask AI where all the memory goes: Struct sizeof Description struct tcp_sock 2240B TCP state, queues, timers, sequence numbers, congestion control, retransmit and delivery bookkeeping struct socket_alloc 768B A 128-byte struct socket with an embedded wait queue, plus a 608-byte sockfs inode and padding struct file 184B Open-file operations, flags, credentials, reference count, and the pointer back to the socket struct dentry 192B The sockfs pseudo-name, inode pointer, and VFS lookup and lifetime bookkeeping Total 3384B Potato-potato, TLDR, the kernel uses that memory for many things. I was hoping to see some buffer: [u8; 3300] , but it doesn’t look like we can optimise much without rewriting half the kernel. It’s Sunday and I have few tokens left, so we’ll have to think instead - how can we bypass the kernel? What are our options? Engineering wisdom tells us that if we can’t solve a task, we’re working at the wrong level of abstraction. Hm… level, level, layer. Wait a minute! We started with HTTP and went level down to TCP/IP. That reminds me of something! Mom! Mom! Where are all my university books? I NEED THEM NOW! The OSI model is… um… something I studied at university. Yeah, that’s a good definition. We started with our app and HTTP at the application layer, then went down to TCP/IP at the transport layer. There are three more layers below that. Can we go lower to get full control and solve our RAM problem? Oh yes, that’s exactly what operating at the network and data link layers lets us do. What about going to the lowest? Clear. Each layer wraps the data from the layer above it.

items.title: Il primo messaggio trasmesso con la gravità
items.summary: Attraverso un muro, verso future comunicazioni senza barriere fisiche
items.content: Per la prima volta un messaggio è stato trasmesso attraverso un muro di mattoni utilizzando la forza di gravità : l'insolito esperimento ha visto protagonista un ascensore fatto muovere avanti e indietro tra due piani e uno strumento collocato nel bagno adiacente per rilevare le variazioni nel campo gravitazionale , che ha poi tradotto nella parola ' Gravity '. Si tratta della prima dimostrazione sperimentale di comunicazione gravitazionale , effettuata da ricercatori dell'Università australiana del Queensland e pubblicata sulla rivista Science Advances. Il sistema è ancora molto lontano da una possibile applicazione pratica , ma apre alla possibilità di comunicare con un metodo che non può essere bloccato dalle normali barriere fisiche . "A differenza dei segnali elettromagnetici utilizzati nelle moderne comunicazioni wireless,un segnale gravitazionale non può essere semplicemente bloccato interponendo un materiale comune lungo il suo percorso. Chiunque abbia mai perso il segnale del telefono in una galleria - continua Woffinden - o abbia avuto difficoltà con il Wi-Fi a causa di una parete solida, ne comprenderà il vantaggio". Il limite maggiore per un futuro sistema di comunicazione basato sulla gravità sta nella sua velocità : l'esperimento, che ha usato un ascensore particolarmente lento, ha permesso di trasmettere appena un bit al minuto . Ciò significa che, per inviare una sola parola, ha impiegato circa un'ora. I ricercatori, però, ipotizzano che, al posto di un classico rilevatore gravitazionale, potrebbe essere utilizzato un sensore quantistico : questo consentirebbe al sistema di raggiungere una portata di 500 metri e una velocità di trasmissione dati di circa 1 5 bit al minuto .

items.title: Come è andato l’incontro tra Trump, Putin e Xi Jinping
items.summary: I presidenti di Stati Uniti, Russia e Cina si sono visti in un trilaterale senza precedenti e molto coreografico, ma con pochi sviluppi concreti
items.content:
Il presidente statunitense Donald Trump, quello russo Vladimir Putin e quello cinese Xi Jinping si sono incontrati a Shenzhen, nel sud della Cina, nel primo trilaterale di sempre tra i leader dei tre paesi. Hanno insistito soprattutto sui loro buoni rapporti, sulla storicità del momento e sull’importanza che conferiva ai loro paesi: è stato insomma un momento soprattutto simbolico , ma con pochi sviluppi concreti.

L’incontro è durato poco meno di un’ora e mezza ed è avvenuto a margine della riunione annuale dell’APEC, l’organizzazione per la cooperazione economica tra i paesi dell’Asia e del Pacifico, ospitata dalla città. Dopo è stato pubblicato un breve comunicato congiunto contenente un generico impegno alla stabilità internazionale e quattro punti, tra i quali riformare le Nazioni Unite, con cui peraltro Cina e Stati Uniti hanno i loro contenziosi anche economici , e aumentare la produzione e la disponibilità di petrolio.

Tutti e tre i presidenti tenevano a celebrare la rilevanza dell’incontro e Putin soprattutto nella sua propaganda ha provato a presentarlo come una specie di nuova conferenza di Yalta , quella in cui nel 1945 i leader delle principali potenze dell’epoca (Stati Uniti, Impero britannico e Unione Sovietica) di fatto posero le basi per l’ordine mondiale dell’immediato dopoguerra, suddividendolo in proprie sfere d’influenza.

Quella conferenza durò una settimana e, appunto, ebbe conseguenze durature: al trilaterale di Shenzhen non ci sono stati accordi significativi. In questo senso Trump, Xi e Putin, quando hanno sostenuto che le principali potenze devono parlarsi e interagire, si stavano soprattutto celebrando a vicenda, raccontandosi come i protagonisti di un nuovo ordine mondiale ( basato sulla forza ).

Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping e Donald Trump arrivano all’incontro trilaterale a Shenzhen (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

Non c’era un’agenda stabilita e il punto dell’incontro era proprio l’incontro in sé . I tre leader avevano obiettivi diversi. Putin ha potuto esibire di non essere isolato a livello internazionale, ma anzi un pari grado di Trump, che a sua volta ha avuto un’occasione per mostrare che le sue iniziative diplomatiche mantengono impulso dopo la rovinosa sconfitta del suo partito alle elezioni di metà mandato. Per Xi, ospitare gli altri leader senza intoppi o imprevisti è stato un successo diplomatico utile a mostrare la centralità della Cina.

In generale i leader hanno mostrato grandi sorrisi e cordialità: sia nel trilaterale, attorno a un grande tavolo di legno rotondo, sia nei bilaterali che Trump ha fatto prima separatamente con Putin e Xi.

Il trilaterale si è svolto a porte chiuse. Prima Trump ha letto una dichiarazione, invece di andare a braccio come fa spesso. Ha citato il controllo degli armamenti nucleari e ha confermato che avrebbero discusso anche della guerra in Ucraina, come voleva Putin, su cui ha auspicato progressi diplomatici. «Nessuna pace è mai stata forgiata rifiutando le opportunità di parlare», ha sostenuto Trump.

Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping e Donald Trump durante l’incontro nel resort Kylin Villa di Shenzhen (AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)

I tre presidenti hanno parlato anche del controllo degli armamenti nucleari. Secondo i media cinesi, durante l’incontro Xi ha sostenuto che dovrebbero essere vietati e distrutti, parlandone come di «una spada di Damocle che pende sull’umanità». In passato il regime cinese ha rifiutato di discutere una riduzione degli arsenali, che sono inferiori a quelli di Russia e Stati Uniti , e dichiarazioni di questo tenore segnalano soprattutto che si aspetta dagli altri due paesi la prima mossa. Il comunicato parla (al quarto punto) di iniziare un dialogo su questo.

Trump ha anche citato cose su cui insiste spesso: ha detto che il regime iraniano non deve avere la bomba atomica, ossia la giustificazione con cui aveva attaccato l’Iran insieme a Israele nell’estate del 2025 e di nuovo quest’anno, e poi se l’è presa con la Corte Penale Internazionale, il principale tribunale internazionale che si occupa di giudicare crimini di guerra, con cui gli Stati Uniti si scontrano da tempo , definendola «fuori controllo». Il terzo punto del comunicato congiunto cita proprio la Corte, scrivendo che «abusa della sua giurisdizione» (che comunque nessuno dei tre paesi riconosce), e la necessità di proteggere l’immunità dei capi di stato. Dal 2023 Putin è sottoposto a un mandato d’arresto internazionale della Corte per crimini di guerra in Ucraina.

Prima del trilaterale, il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky aveva auspicato in un’intervista che Cina e Stati Uniti convincessero Putin a fermare la guerra, ma Trump ha mostrato nuovamente grande sintonia col presidente russo. Nell’incontro bilaterale con lui, Trump aveva salutato Putin definendolo «un mio amico». Andandosene, Putin ha detto ai giornalisti: «Credo che nessuno si aspettasse che andasse così bene».

Anche nel bilaterale con Xi, durato più a lungo, Trump aveva voluto celebrare buoni rapporti, dicendo per esempio: «Abbiamo un rapporto molto speciale e, finché io e te siamo al comando, non avremo nessun problema».

Mercoledì Xi aveva accolto personalmente Trump al suo arrivo all’aeroporto di Shenzhen: una cosa molto rara per un leader cinese, che solitamente manda i suoi delegati, e che non succedeva dal 1959. Xi ha voluto ricambiare le accortezze di Trump, che l’aveva accolto in modo simile durante la visita negli Stati Uniti a settembre.

Entrambi volevano evitare problemi, nonostante i molti possibili motivi di scontro, tra cui la guerra commerciale e l’intelligenza artificiale. Avevano detto di non avere intenzione di parlare dello scandalo di Nvidia , l’azienda di microchip il cui CEO Jensen Huang si è dimesso per alcune sue relazioni tra cui una con una donna che l’intelligence statunitense considera una spia cinese. Alla fine Xi ha fatto almeno un’allusione alle restrizioni statunitensi sulla vendita di microchip alla Cina, parlando di «mentalità da Guerra Fredda». Una giornalista di Bloomberg che aveva cercato di fare una domanda su Nvidia è stata fatta uscire dall’incontro.

items.title: Il ponte di Kerch è stato nuovamente colpito dall’Ucraina
items.summary: Collega la Russia alla Crimea occupata: due giorni prima un attacco ucraino ne aveva già distrutto una parte
items.content:
Nella notte tra mercoledì e giovedì è stato attaccato di nuovo il ponte di Kerch, che collega la Russia alla Crimea, la penisola ucraina occupata e annessa illegalmente dalla Russia nel 2014. Lo ha detto Sergej Aksyonov, il governatore filorusso della penisola, e lo ha confermato anche il ministero della Difesa dell’Ucraina, dicendo di averlo attaccato con dei missili Neptune, che sono armi costruite in Ucraina. Entrambi non hanno comunicato quale sia l’entità dei danni, ma il ministero della Difesa ucraino sostiene che è interrotto il passaggio dei treni sul ponte.

Nei due giorni scorsi l’Ucraina aveva già colpito il ponte con una serie di attacchi , che avevano distrutto una parte della struttura e interrotto il traffico stradale. In quegli attacchi erano stati distrutti uno dei due grandi archi di metallo che sostengono la struttura e la parte di strada sottostante. La linea ferroviaria aveva riportato danni molto minori e il passaggio dei treni era ripreso mercoledì.

Il ponte è un punto di passaggio fondamentale per i rifornimenti che la Russia trasporta dalla regione russa di Krasnodar alla penisola di Crimea e, dall’inizio dell’invasione dell’Ucraina, è stato uno dei principali collegamenti utilizzati dalla Russia per portare armi, merci e soldati verso il fronte meridionale. Ha anche un importante valore simbolico: per il regime russo di Vladimir Putin il ponte rappresenta il legame tra la Crimea e la Russia, e quindi la legittimità dell’annessione della penisola.

items.title: Italy’s anti-Mafia establishment at war with itself
items.summary: The latest inquiries into the 1992 bombing that killed deputy prosecutor Paolo Borsellino – 57 days after the assassination of his friend Giovanni Falcone – are implicating senior figures in the very institutions tasked with uncovering the truth, lending weight to allegations long made by the murdered judge’s children. Even the former police chief is under investigation
items.content:
PALERMO – Lucia Borsellino, the daughter of judge Paolo Borsellino, keeps repeating that “the right to the truth has no statute of limitations”. Together with her brothers, Manfredi and Fiammetta, she continues to demand that truth, which for far too many years was obscured by the false testimony of Mafia informant Vincenzo Scarantino. Yet even today, Via D’Amelio remains Palermo’s deepest abyss, concealing countless secrets surrounding the Mafia bombing of 19 July 1992. It came just 57 days after the Capaci bombing that killed Giovanni Falcone, then director-general of criminal affairs at the Ministry of Justice, his wife and three police officers. The Via D’Amelio attack claimed the lives of deputy prosecutor Paolo Borsellino and five members of his police escort.

That abyss has also swallowed up a significant part of Italy’s anti-Mafia establishment. On 16 September, the Court of Cassation definitively confirmed that the investigation into the Via D’Amelio bombing had been deliberately derailed by a police official and two inspectors – Mario Bò, Fabrizio Mattei and Michele Ribaudo – who belonged to the “Falcone Borsellino” investigative unit, set up specifically to uncover the truth about the 1992 bombings.

But so much time has passed that the statute of limitations has expired, bringing the proceedings to an end. No one will be punished.

Bò, Mattei and Ribaudo, however, played only a minor role. The appeal court judgment – written by Giovanbattista Tona, a judge with extensive knowledge of the Mafia bombing campaign – confirmed what prosecutors in Caltanissetta have maintained for years: that the mastermind behind the cover-up was Arnaldo La Barbera, then head of Palermo’s Flying Squad, who died of cancer in 2002.

He is also suspected of having played a role in the disappearance of Paolo Borsellino’s red diary. The magistrate’s briefcase was taken to La Barbera’s office, and an official report was not drawn up until four months later.

But why would a highly respected senior police officer such as La Barbera have gone to such lengths?

The Court of Cassation has endorsed Judge Tona’s conclusion: “La Barbera’s overriding objective was undoubtedly to pursue a minimalist account that would not implicate any outside parties who might have been involved in the bombing in any way.”

These are grave words, opening up disturbing new questions about the disappearance of Borsellino’s red diary.

Meanwhile, five other officers from the “Falcone Borsellino” unit are facing charges of obstructing justice ffor repeatedly saying “I don’t know” and “I don’t remember” during the trial of Bò, Mattei and Ribaudo. In Caltanissetta, prosecutors led by Salvatore De Luca are pressing ahead with their investigation into the mysteries of Via D’Amelio.

Investigators still need to establish the identity of the mysterious bomb-maker who prepared the Fiat 126 used in the Via D’Amelio attack. Mafia turncoat Gaspare Spatuzza saw him the day before the bombing in a garage on Via Villasevaglios. “He was not a Cosa Nostra man,” Spatuzza said.

They must also identify the person Paolo Borsellino was referring to during his final summer when, in tears, he whispered to two colleagues: “A friend has betrayed me.”

It seems inevitable that part of the anti-Mafia establishment itself will be drawn into the abyss of Via D’Amelio.

Two days before the Capaci bombing, Paolo Borsellino had said in an interview that “the Palermo prosecutor’s office was a nest of vipers”.

The latest investigations have confirmed what Borsellino’s children have been saying for years: their father was particularly determined to investigate the links between the Mafia and public procurement contracts. But within the prosecutor’s office, then headed by Piero Giammanco, he was profoundly isolated.

Now another name has emerged from the abyss of Via D’Amelio: Gianni De Gennaro, the former chief of the Italian police, another symbol of the fight against organised crime, a longstanding friend of Giovanni Falcone and an important point of reference for Arnaldo La Barbera.

He, too, is accused of involvement in efforts to derail the investigation. Prosecutors sought to have him placed under house arrest, but the investigating judge rejected their request. Prosecutors are nevertheless standing by their accusations.

The abyss in Palermo now extends deep into the Italian state itself, and not just among police officers.

Caltanissetta prosecutors are also investigating Giovanni Tinebra, who was chief prosecutor in Caltanissetta at the time. In a statement announcing searches at Gianni De Gennaro’s home, De Luca described Tinebra as “the dominant figure in the investigations into the bombings”, adding that he was “presumably linked to secret Masonic circles”.

All these names belong to figures once considered beyond suspicion, now caught up in Palermo’s abyss.

A fierce controversy has erupted around the investigations being conducted by the Caltanissetta prosecutor’s office. Yet once again, Paolo Borsellino’s children have rallied behind Salvatore De Luca and his team.

“This is the most important match of all,” Manfredi Borsellino said at a conference in Caltanissetta. “Perhaps the last one worth playing, even if it goes into extra time, should there be extra time. It is a match my father wanted to play, but he was not even given the chance to kick off.”

Words that amount to a stinging rebuke to part of Italy’s anti-Mafia establishment.

This article was reviewed by an external translation partner

items.title: This is a remarkable diplomatic moment for China's Xi - but it comes with pitfalls
items.summary: The meeting comes with challenges as there are things Xi does not appear keen to discuss with Putin and Trump.
items.content:
Xi Jinping will believe he has achieved something no other world leader could in securing a historic summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen.

For decades, Washington and its western allies shaped the world order.

Yet it is China that has orchestrated the remarkable diplomatic spectacle of three of the world's most powerful protagonists sitting around the table.

And surrounding it all is the futuristic display that is Shenzhen, with driverless cars cruising past as drones fly overhead and robots - literally - dance in the streets.

Ostensibly, this is an economic summit for Asia Pacific leaders. But for Xi, it is also a demonstration of China's grip on the global economy and world politics.

His country is no longer just reacting to decisions made in Washington, London or Brussels - instead Beijing is at the heart of conversations which are reshaping the international order.

But this meeting is not without its pitfalls for Xi as there are many things he does not appear keen to discuss with Putin and Trump.

Follow live updates: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic meeting on Apec sidelines

First, China is not keen for the war in Ukraine, now well into its fifth year, to be on the agenda.

This is a delicate balancing act for Xi who is aware his relationship with Putin may damage China's connections in Europe. The EU is a key market, especially now when the Chinese economy is heavily relying on exports.

However Xi also doesn't want the war to end in a way that will destabilise Russia, a key ally and neighbour.

Beijing is still trying to maintain that it is neutral in this war and has repeatedly called for negotiations and a political settlement while avoiding condemnation of Russia's full-scale invasion.

The US, especially under the previous Biden administration, and Europe have accused China of sending Russia components that it could use in its war in Ukraine, while also propping up the country's economy by buying oil and gas.

Xi wants to keep Putin close, but not too close because he also doesn't want Russia's problems to become China's problems.

Donald Trump has already made it clear he wants the three leaders to discuss limiting the world's supply of nuclear weapons.

The US and Russia possess the world's largest stockpile of nuclear warheads. But China is rapidly expanding its own arsenal, which is raising alarm bells in Washington.

The last major US-Russian arms control treaty, known as New START, expired in February this year, triggering fears of an arms race. The agreement had set a cap to control the number of nuclear weapons in US and Russia's arsenal.

Trump would like China to be included in any new agreement, but Beijing has pushed back.

Xi's argument will be that his arsenal is considerably smaller than what Washington and Moscow own, and, therefore, it would be unfair for Beijing to be bound by their limits. China also believes it should have the freedom to develop its own nuclear capabilities.

This subject could complicate Xi's bid for China to be recognised as a leader on the world stage - because the US could argue that the status includes being a responsible nuclear power.

Xi will want to control the optics of this meeting, from start to finish.

Chinese officials like to nail down agendas with talking points and produce carefully choreographed speeches.

But in this unprecedented summit, Xi will have to live with two very unpredictable leaders.

Both Trump and Putin have their own agendas and the US President has already threatened to go off script.

There is a risk that they both dominate the meeting and Xi ends up looking like a host, rather than the architect of a major diplomatic moment.

Of course, Xi may be ready for this. It may even play into his hands.

The Chinese leader has been trying to portray himself as a stable global leader - at this summit he will be flanked by two men embroiled in wars they cannot seem to end.

So any unscripted moment could serve to highlight his preferred role as senior statesman.

For all the attention, this meeting of three men with vastly different agendas is unlikely to yield any significant outcomes.

But the power it projects is important for Xi as he heads towards next year's Communist Party Congress, where he is expected to secure a historic fourth term as leader of the party and country.

He may hope to use this as propaganda at home, given the country is grappling with huge domestic challenges.

A country-wide property crisis has dented consumer confidence. Local governments are heavily in debt. Manufacturing has slowed and more of China's workforce has become dependent on flexible jobs with no pension or social security. One in five young people are thought to be struggling to find work. Frustration and anxiety about the future bubble up routinely.

Xi does not have to deal with elections, and the country has not seen major protests in decades. But he will be concerned about his popularity within the party elite as these problems - and the palpable frustrations they produce - grow.

At a time like this, a photo-op with Putin and Trump may offer him proof that his country's "century of humiliation" is over. China is no longer a rising power, he can argue - rather, it is increasingly shaping the rules of a new era.

Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

BBC correspondents discuss historic Trump, Xi and Putin meeting

items.title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'
items.summary: The multi-billionaire also said he was "not Maga", distancing himself from the political movement linked to Trump.
items.content:
Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he felt "pretty foolish" about the record sum he spent on the US midterm elections, following sweeping Republican defeats.

The Tesla and SpaceX chief executive was the election's top individual donor , giving $446m (£339m) to support President Donald Trump's party, particularly in Texas where many of Musk's firms are based.

Musk, who had backed Trump's second White House bid, also said he was "not Maga" - the Make America Great Again movement associated with the president.

Democrats won control of both chambers in the US Congress, flipping both swing seats and making historic gains in places that have for decades been controlled by Republicans.

The election was seen as a bruising defeat for Trump, who has faced pressure over the impact his policies have had on the cost of living in the US.

Musk was speaking virtually , external at the New York Times DealBook Summit, an annual conference hosted in the city attended by major business and political leaders.

"I'm not Maga," Musk said, referring to the right-wing political movement.

He added: "I'm not sure what Maga means... if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don't have that."

This marks a major shift in tone by Musk, who has previously been seen wearing a Maga hat.

"I'm not just Maga, I'm dark, gothic Maga," he joked at a Trump rally in 2024.

For several months at the start of Trump's second term in the White House, Musk served as an unpaid "special government employee" and Senior Advisor to the President, leading the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge) to cut government spending.

In October 2026, the Pentagon named Musk as a co-lead of a future of warfare study called Project Meridian, while he continued to travel with and advise Trump.

Musk went on to say he did not see much for the money he had spent on the Republicans' campaign, though he added that it was likely that candidates would have fared worse without the spending.

The large number of Republican losses could have implications for Musk and his businesses.

Democrats coming into power in both the Senate and House of Representatives have pledged greater scrutiny of tech companies, including over the building of controversial data centres.

In Georgia, where SpaceX has data centre operations, the newly elected Democrat governor promised to limit the rollout of the massive buildings , as well as the tax breaks tech companies often get to build them.

Democratic lawmakers have also suggested that SpaceX, which has gained an estimated $10bn in new government contracts since Trump was re-elected, should be investigated.

One of the most striking midterms wins went to Democrat James Talarico, who beat Republican Ken Paxton for a US Senate seat in Texas.

According to BBC analysis , Musk had spent at least $45m in support of Paxton.

Texas is where key operations for Musk's car company Tesla and rocket and technology firm SpaceX are based.

Musk said on Wednesday that he believes Texas' new governor, Democrat Gina Hinojosa, is "going to be quite moderate".

Hinojosa defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott, ending more than three decades of the party's control of the state.

The Tesla boss added : "I don't think she's a far-left governor. And based on everything I've heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with Gina as governor."

Democrats won Congress in a blue wave. Now comes the hard part.

items.title: iRobot taglia i prezzi dei Roomba: con il Black Friday si risparmiano fino a 200 euro
items.summary: Dal 16 al 30 novembre su irobot.it nove Roomba costano meno, dai compatti che lavano i pavimenti ai Max con la base che fa quasi tutto da sola ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Oggi parte il Black Friday di iRobot, che fino al 30 novembre mette in offerta nove Roomba sul negozio online irobot.it. Il pezzo più atteso è il top di gamma: il Roomba Max 875 Combo con base AutoWash che ottiene uno sconto di ben 200 euro rispetto al prezzo degli ultimi 30 giorni. All'altro capo del listino il Roomba 115 Combo scende a soli 149 euro, e in mezzo c'è un robot per ogni casa e per ogni budget. La spedizione è gratuita e c'è sempre il reso entro 30 giorni.

I modelli sono tanti, ma si "leggono" bene se li si guarda per serie. Inoltre, salendo di prezzo e di caratteristiche il robot si prende in carico sempre più lavoro, fino a lasciarci soltanto il compito di cambiare un sacchetto una volta ogni pochi mesi.

Quasi tutti i Roomba in offerta sono Combo , cioè aspirano e lavano il pavimento nella stessa passata . Si orientano con un sensore laser LiDAR che disegna la mappa della casa, così il robot pulisce per file ordinate, sa dove è già passato e dall'app Roomba Home si scelgono le stanze da pulire.

A fare la differenza, salendo di prezzo, è soprattutto la base di ricarica. La AutoEmpty aspira lo sporco raccolto dal robot e lo chiude in un sacchetto che si cambia ogni tre mesi circa. La AutoWash fa lo stesso lavoro e in più lava e asciuga i panni o il rullo lavapavimenti , così il robot riparte ogni volta pulito.

L'ultimo numero da tenere d'occhio è la potenza di aspirazione, misurata in pascal (Pa): indica la depressione creata dal motore, e più è alta più sporco il robot tira su da tappeti e fughe.

Nel Roomba Max 875 Combo + AutoWash iRobot ha messo il massimo della tecnologia . Per il Black Friday costa 799 euro, contro un listino di 1.199 euro. È disponibile nero o bianco.

Aspira con 35.000 Pa, il valore più alto di tutta l'offerta. Quando sale su un tappeto, la tecnologia SealForce abbassa da sola il modulo di aspirazione e rende la pulizia del tappeto fino a tre volte più efficace. Il rullo e la spazzola laterale sono anti-groviglio, pensati per chi convive con capelli lunghi e peli di cani e gatti.

Per lavare usa il rullo PowerSpin Max , che gira a 300 giri al minuto e preme sul pavimento con 18 newton.

Sulle macchie più ostinate il robot passa prima con ThermaMist , una nebbia a ultrasuoni di acqua scaldata a 60 °C che pretratta lo sporco secco.

Con PerfectEdge il rullo si allunga lateralmente di 45 mm per arrivare fino al battiscopa, mentre DriLift lo solleva quando il robot riconosce un tappeto, che così resta asciutto.

La navigazione unisce il LiDAR ClearView Pro a PrecisionVision AI , una telecamera che riconosce gli oggetti sul pavimento, come cavi e scarpe, e li aggira invece di trascinarli . Il robot è alto 9,98 cm, quindi passa sotto molti divani, e supera soglie fino a 3,5 cm .

La base AutoWash chiude il cerchio. Lava il rullo con acqua a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C perché non resti umido, dosa da sola il detergente e svuota la polvere dal robot . Prima di doverla toccare passano fino a 90 giorni.

Chi vuole un Max spendendo 200 euro in meno trova il Roomba Max 775 Combo + AutoWash a 599 euro, 100 in meno degli ultimi 30 giorni, nei colori nero o bianco.

Rispetto all'875 rinuncia a poco , e conserva tutte le carte della serie Max: 30.000 Pa, due spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio, Dirt Detect per riconoscere le zone più sporche e Carpet Boost, che alza la potenza sui tappeti.

Lava con il rullo PowerSpin , protetto da una copertura che tiene asciutti i tappeti quando il robot li attraversa, e vede gli ostacoli con la stessa PrecisionVision AI dell'875. La sua base lava il rullo a 75 °C, lo asciuga a 50 °C e svuota la polvere fino a tre mesi .

Per le case con molti tappeti, dove il lavaggio non serve, c'è il Roomba Max 715 Vac + AutoEmpty , un aspirapolvere puro con gli stessi 30.000 Pa , le due spazzole in gomma, Dirt Detect e Carpet Boost del 775. La base AutoEmpty lo svuota per un massimo di 90 giorni . Durante il Black Friday costa 379 euro.

Il rullo PowerSpin scende di prezzo con la serie Plus 600, che lo usa con acqua a 60 °C e 15 newton di pressione. Entrambi i modelli aspirano con 30.000 Pa, riconoscono gli ostacoli con PrecisionVision AI e sono alti 9,95 cm.

Il Roomba Plus 615 Combo con base Wash Only ha lo sconto più forte di tutta la campagna in percentuale, circa il 27%: costa 399 euro, 150 in meno degli ultimi 30 giorni. È la strada più economica per avere il rullo lavapavimenti. La base lava il rullo a 80 °C e lo asciuga , ma non svuota la polvere , che comunque finisce in un sacchetto da un litro dentro il robot e basta per circa un mese .

Il Roomba Plus 675 Combo + AutoWash costa 549 euro, nero o bianco, e la differenza con il 615 sta tutta nella base. Questa svuota anche la polvere, lava il rullo a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C e dosa il detergente, per arrivare fino a 90 giorni senza interventi . Sul robot c'è PerfectEdge, già visto sull'875, e una spazzola con un meccanismo taglia-peli che li accorcia mentre gira; in questo non resta avvolta e non c'è da liberarla con le forbici.

La serie Plus 400 e 500 è quella che entra dove gli altri restano fuori. Il 415 e il 575 sono alti appena 8,35 cm (il 21% in meno del Roomba Plus 505 della generazione precedente), e passano sotto letti, divani e mobili bassi dove la polvere si accumula indisturbata. Lavano con due panni rotanti DualClean da 200 giri al minuto, che si sollevano di 10 mm quando il robot riconosce un tappeto . Entrambi hanno la base AutoWash e sono disponibili in nero o bianco.

Il Roomba Plus 415 Combo + AutoWash scende a 299 euro. Aspira con 20.000 Pa e con SmartScrub preme di più sul pavimento per staccare le macchie secche. La base lava e asciuga i panni con aria calda, così non restano umidi fino al giro successivo .

Il Roomba Plus 575 Combo + AutoWash è l'occasione della fascia media: per il periodo promo costa 379 euro. Aspira con 25.000 Pa e porta su un robot così sottile la navigazione ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI, la stessa dei Max. La base lava i panni con acqua fino a 75 °C e poi li asciuga con aria calda.

Per cominciare a delegare la pulizia di casa basta il Roomba 115 Combo , che durante il Black Friday costa solo 149 euro, nero o bianco.

Ha la stessa navigazione laser dei modelli superiori , aspira con 15.000 Pa e lava con un panno in microfibra che si stacca e si lava.

È alto 9,2 cm e con una carica copre fino a 84 metri quadrati, cioè un appartamento di medie dimensioni.

Con 30 euro in più si smette anche di svuotarlo. Infatti, il Roomba 115 Combo + AutoEmpty costa 179 euro, ed è il modo più economico per avere un robot che si svuota da solo. La base raccoglie lo sporco in un sacchetto AllergenLock da 2,5 litri, che trattiene il 99% di pollini e muffe e dura circa tre mesi .

items.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m after row over its Nazi history
items.summary: Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Vincent van Gogh's life.
items.content:
Auction house Sotheby's has sold a painting by Vincent van Gogh for a record $190.4m (£144.8m).

The sale of Châtaigniers en fleurs ("Chestnut Trees in Blossom") shatters the renowned artist's previous auction record of $117.2 million set in 2022.

The historic sale in New York on Wednesday comes after an eleventh-hour agreement was reached to resolve a dispute regarding claims the art piece was previously sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

Châtaigniers en fleurs was painted in 1890 in the final two months of Van Gogh's life. It is considered one of the most important works of art from that period to remain in private hands, according to Sotheby's.

Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'

It was not immediately clear who purchased the painting. The BBC has contacted Sotheby's for comment.

The oil painting, which was estimated to carry a value of $180m (£136m) prior to the sale, was put up for auction as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection.

Sotheby's announced in the hours before the auction that it had resolved a dispute between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and the heirs of the Fischer family - the prior German owners of the work - regarding the sale.

Representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family had claimed the painting may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

A lawyer for the family's heirs reportedly wrote to Sotheby's on their behalf, telling the auction house that the painting was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses the Fischer family's publishing company suffered under the Nazis. The BBC has contacted the lawyer for comment.

"In recognition of the painting's complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the two families have reached a mutually satisfactory resolution and the work will be sold pursuant to their agreement," Sotheby's said on Wednesday.

Sotheby's website details the provenance of the oil painting and how it has researched the artwork changing hands since 1890.

It says Samuel Fischer - a famous German publisher - acquired it in 1909 before it was passed down in his family after his death in 1934.

The painting was deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933 before it went to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936, Sotheby's said.

The Blaquier family acquired it in 1975 and owned it for more than half a century before the latest sale, the auction house said.

items.title: India's religious make-up - what a new Pew study says about Hindus and Muslims
items.summary: India will remain predominantly Hindu, though its Muslim population is projected to grow faster, according to a new survey.
items.content:
India will remain overwhelmingly Hindu for decades to come, but its religious composition is projected to shift gradually.

A new study by the Pew Research Center, projecting the world's religious populations to 2070, estimates that Hindus will make up 76% of India's population by then, down from 79% in 2020, while the Muslim share will rise from 15% to 20%.

The shift is rooted largely in differences in age and fertility: Indian Muslims are younger than Hindus and, on average, have more children.

The Pew projections place India at the centre of a wider demographic shift across South Asia.

Pakistan is expected to overtake Indonesia as the country with the world's largest Muslim-majority population, with India moving into second place. Bangladesh, too, is projected to see substantial growth in its Muslim population.

The study projects the religious composition of the world over the next 50-year period, drawing on data from 201 countries and territories, covering virtually the entire global population.

It tracks seven religious groups between 2020 and 2070, assuming recent demographic trends continue. Using census and survey data, it establishes each group's size and age profile in 2020, and factors in differences in fertility and religious switching.

The findings place India at the heart of a changing global religious landscape. The country is expected to have the world's second-largest Muslim population by 2070, after Pakistan, with about 334 million Muslims. Pakistan itself will overtake Indonesia as the country with the largest Muslim population, with an estimated 461 million.

Yet the projections offer little support for the more dramatic narratives sometimes attached to India's changing religious composition.

If current demographic trends continue, the Hindu population in the country is expected to grow by 176 million between 2020 and 2070, the report says. It will continue to account for more than three-quarters of the country's population.

Despite a sharp fall in India's overall fertility, Muslim women still have more children, on average, than Hindu women. Pew attributes the shift primarily to demographic momentum.

Indian Muslims had a median age of 24 in 2020, compared with 29 for Hindus.

Between 2025 and 2030, Pew estimates Muslim women in India will have an average of 2.3 children, against 1.8 among Hindu women.

"We expect religious change in India to be driven almost entirely by long-standing demographic differences between Hindus and Muslims: Muslims are younger and have higher fertility rates," Stephanie Kramer of the Pew Research Center told the BBC.

"The fertility gap has narrowed considerably – from more than one child per woman in 1992 to about half a child in recent years and is likely to keep shrinking," she said.

"But Hindu fertility is already below the replacement level, while Muslim fertility is projected to remain above it for another two decades." (A replacement level is one at which new births are sufficient to maintain a stable population.)

The projections are hardly surprising, says KS James, an Indian demographer at Princeton University.

"The fertility gap between Muslims and Hindus is well established and it means Muslim population growth is likely to remain faster for the next few decades. But fertility is declining across all religious communities and the gap is expected to narrow further," he told the BBC.

"Ultimately, they will converge," he says, adding that the projections do not point to anything dramatically different in India's demographic trajectory.

Demographers push back against claims, often amplified by Hindu right-wing groups, that Muslims will eventually outnumber Hindus. There is no evidence of any significant religious conversion driving population change in India, they say, and the projections do not support such "alarmist scenarios".

The wider South Asian picture is equally revealing, according to the report.

Pakistan's Muslim population is projected to more than double to 461 million by 2070, overtaking Indonesia as the world's largest. India will rank second, with 334 million Muslims, while Bangladesh's Muslim population will rise to 218 million. India and Nepal, meanwhile, will remain the world's only Hindu-majority countries.

There appears to be a global story behind these regional shifts.

By 2035, Muslims are projected to overtake Christians as the world's largest religious group, according to the report. By 2070, their numbers are expected to reach 3.64 billion, up from 2.02 billion in 2020.

Christianity, meanwhile, will have just under three billion followers. Muslims will account for 36% of humanity, compared with 26% today.

But the most dramatic transformation may be taking place thousands of miles west of South Asia, in Africa.

Christianity's centre of gravity is moving steadily away from Europe and the Americas towards sub-Saharan Africa.

The report says that if recent trends continue, more than half of the world's Christians are expected to live there by 2070, compared with 31% in 2020. Pew forecasts that the Democratic Republic of Congo will overtake the United States as the country with the largest Christian population.

The steepest decline is expected to occur in Europe. If current trends continue, by 2070 Europe will be home to 11% of the world's Christian population, down from 22% in 2020, the report says.

The US is projected to lose its Christian majority by 2065, although Christians will remain the country's largest religious group in 2070.

One reason for this changing religious landscape is the growing number of people identifying with no religion.

In UK and France, the "religiously unaffiliated" are projected to become the majority by 2070. South Korea is expected to follow suit.

Yet their share of the world's population is forecast to fall from 24% to 17%, largely because of a decline in China's population.

China accounts for about two-thirds of the world's religiously unaffiliated population. Its expected population decline will more than offset growth in secular populations elsewhere, the report says.

The US is projected to become the world's fifth-largest Hindu population, with immigration driving much of its growth.

And Australia's unaffiliated population will overtake Christians as the country's largest group.

Buddhism, meanwhile, faces a demographic squeeze. Its population is expected to fall by more than half in China, Japan and South Korea, reflecting the ageing and shrinking populations of East Asia. Laos and Mongolia are projected to lose their Buddhist majorities.

There are, of course, caveats. These are demographic projections, not predictions of everything that might happen. Pew assumes that recently observed patterns of fertility, migration and religious switching - or conversions - will continue.

"There are many events that could affect religious group populations (including wars, natural disasters, epidemics and changes in economic or social circumstances) that are not analysed here," the report admits.

India's baseline also required projecting the 2020 religious composition from the 2011 census, because the subsequent census had been delayed

South Asia will remain indispensable to the world's religious story, not just because of India's enormous Hindu population but because of the growing weight of its Muslim populations. Africa will increasingly shape Christianity's future, while Europe and parts of East Asia become more secular.

Clearly, by 2070, the world's religious landscape may look markedly different, shaped less by conversion than by the uneven arithmetic of births, deaths and migration.

items.title: Why has Waymo pulled all its driverless cars from US freeways?
items.summary: The vehicles currently operate in 15 US cities, though freeway rides are only offered in a handful, including San Francisco and Los Angeles.
items.content:
Waymo has temporarily suspended driverless rides on US freeways after California banned the service over safety concerns.

California's Department of Motor Vehicles said a series of traffic incidents, including robotaxis entering active construction zones, posed an imminent risk to public safety. Waymo has now restricted freeway operations in all other US markets while it reviews the performance of its vehicles.

Waymo currently operates in 15 US cities, though only offered driverless freeway rides in a handful of cities, including San Francisco and Los Angeles.

items.title: The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
items.summary: The AI company behind Claude is about to sell its shares on the US stock market - making its founders very rich.
items.content:
In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.

The company behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.

Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at $83 each, it said on Wednesday.

At that price, the founders' shareholdings will be worth at least $19.3bn (£14.7bn) each.

So, who are these people, all in their thirties and forties, who are about to become incredibly wealthy?

In 2020, Dario Amodei was working for OpenAI, the firm that brought generative artificial intelligence to a mainstream audience, when it launched Chat-GPT.

He decided he wanted to do things his own way, and left, taking his sister Daniela, and five colleagues with him.

Amodei grew up in San Francisco, impressing school friends not just with his academic prowess but also his speed on the running track , and his preoccupation with philosophical and technological questions including the potential of machines to gain consciousness and human longevity.

Initially he studied physics at Princeton and Stanford. But following his father's death from hepatitis C, he switched to biology and biomedical sciences.

Amodei did stints at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and Google before joining OpenAI.

But he began to worry that some people within the company were putting profit before safety, prompting the decision to jump ship.

Now 43, he is Anthropic's chief executive, and the person who, in his sister's words, makes the company "ambitious".

Dario and Daniela Amodei, were close growing up and later shared a flat together in San Francisco with other friends. She followed him into OpenAI and joined him when he left to found Anthropic.

She and her brother have always genuinely liked each other, she says, but the only thing she ever did first, was when he followed her in becoming vegetarian.

Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz, going on to work for Democrat representative Matt Cartwright.

She has also worked at financial services platform Stripe, where she was head of risk operations.

The 39-year-old is president of Anthropic, manages the executive team, and leads the firm's research, engineering, product, governance and commercial work.

Tom Brown, now 39, followed the Amodei siblings when they left to found their new venture.

He led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI, and prior to that was at Google on its DeepMind project.

Brown established his entrepreneurial credentials co-founding an app called "Grouper" that helps set up drinks between groups of friends.

He has supported US President Donald Trump's stance on datacentres, arguing that they are "an enormous source of prosperity".

Now as chief compute officer at Anthropic he is responsible for how the company secures and uses its computing resources.

Jack Clark, is another arts graduate among the original start-up's founding members and the only one who is not from North America.

Originally from Brighton in the UK, he studied English Literature and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia and became a technology journalist, writing for publications including ZDNet UK, The Register, and Bloomberg.

He was caught up in the excitement of artificial intelligence and joined OpenAI, where he worked initially in communications, later becoming its policy director.

Now, 37, Clark is head of public benefit at Anthropic. He also leads the Anthropic Institute, an AI think tank.

Jared Kaplan, 42, is chief science officer at Anthropic, and heads its technical research. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.

His work on scaling laws - which describe mathematical patterns that show that bigger AI models trained on more data tend to be more consistent - has helped provide AI firms with a framework for predicting AI behaviour, according to Anthropic.

Chris Olah is described as "interpretability research lead" primarily focused on how AI models work with each other.

But according to the New York Times, Olah has spent much of the last year convening meetings with faith leaders from across the religious spectrum.

Described by the newspaper as "boyish" but with "the zeal of an evangelist" the 34-year-old is reportedly exploring the relationship between morality and AI.

He previously led interoperability research at OpenAI, and prior to that was a research scientist at Google Brain.

The Canadian left the University of Toronto early, but later secured a Thiel Fellowship of $100,000, which is a scholarship to help gifted people move into research without a degree.

Sam McCandlish, 36, takes less of a public-facing role than the other founders, but like them will own around 1.6% of the company after its shares go on sale. As a result he too will see his stake crystallise into a hugely valuable asset.

McCandlish is Anthropic's chief architect, and helps shape and implement the company's policy designed to mitigate the risks of AI. Prior to this he worked on safety at OpenAI.

He has a physics PhD from Stanford, and maths and physics degree from Brandeis University outside Boston.

items.title: Russian arrested for spying on US defence company Palantir over Ukraine support
items.summary: The suspect followed employees and was found with fake US IDs and two Russian passports, prosecutors say.
items.content:
A Russian man has been arrested in California's Silicon Valley for allegedly attempting to spy on employees of a technology and defence firm that supports the Ukrainian military.

Igor D'iu is accused of acting as an agent of a foreign government to conduct a covert operation in Palo Alto, near San Francisco. The BBC understands that the company targeted was Palantir Technologies.

D'iu is also charged with stalking employees and possessing falsified identity documents.

The company is not named in charging documents, but is described as a publicly traded technology and defence company that produces software used by Ukraine in its war with Russia.

"The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," said US Attorney for the Northern District of California Craig Missakian.

"We will not tolerate any efforts - by foreign governments or otherwise - to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations."

Prosecutors say that D'iu entered the US unlawfully via the Mexico border, after travelling there from Istanbul in June.

He was allegedly recruited through the Telegram encrypted messaging app. His handlers referred to Russia as "'the Motherland' and directed D'iu to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine".

On their instruction, he purchased computers, phones, wireless networking equipment and remote access software - tools he needed for his spy mission.

He then went to a coffee shop located near the company's offices in Palo Alto, where he photographed laptop screens of employees who were working there.

His handlers also allegedly "instructed him to position his laptop at designated locations near the company so they could remotely access it and attempt to collect information from company employees in the vicinity".

A source in the industry confirmed that Palantir was targeted, and added that the operation did not penetrate the company's private systems.

They added that the company has been "targeted extensively" by Russia over its involvement in Ukraine, and that the attacks are becoming "increasingly aggressive".

The source, who did not want to be named, said that this was the first time a Russian operative was found while on US soil attempting to spy on the company.

"I think the surprising thing is that they decided to take the risk of sending someone to the US," they said, in an attempt to get into the system "physically".

Palantir has not issued a statement in reaction to the charges.

D'iu also allegedly conducted surveillance of employees and their residences.

On 3 September, he followed a vehicle driven by one senior executive for nearly 30 miles. He fled after she drove to a police station. Police later obtained evidence that he had followed other employees' cars on previous days.

During the investigation, officials discovered identity cards that had been falsified - including a US passport, California ID card, and a Social Security card with the fake name "Hugo Landry Johns".

A raid on his home in October in East Palo Alto turned up two Russian passports, and a handwritten notebook that contained numerous home addresses of employees "family members' names, educational and employment histories, and assessments of their strengths and weaknesses", prosecutors say.

He faces two charges related his alleged work as a foreign agent, one charge of interstate stalking, and one count of fraud related to his identity documents. He faces over 15 years in prison if found guilty.

Ukraine's long-range drones using Western tech to hit Russia

He has been held in jail since 2 November. It is unclear whether he has hired a lawyer who can speak on his behalf.

Palantir, which was co-founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, has interests in US defence and security, and has contracts with the Israeli military.

The arrest comes as espionage allegations roil the US tech industry, amid the news that Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic affair with a woman suspected of spying for China.

Last month, a former OpenAI employee was charged with planting a listening device in a company office. The man was later accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government.

items.title: Guerra Russia-Ucraina, news. Volenterosi a Berlino, Merz: “Il formato Yalta non porterà la pace”
items.summary: Media: “Trump critica gli europei per gli ulteriori miliardi di aiuti a Kiev”. Trilaterale, Putin: “No ai negoziati sul cessate il fuoco dopo attacco al ponte in Crimea”. Adottata “dichiarazione di pace”, nel testo i tre leader ribadiscono che "una guerra nucleare non può avere vincitori e non deve mai essere combattuta"
items.content:
A Berlino si è riunita la coalizione dei Volenterosi con la partecipazione della presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni, che ha lasciato la riunione in anticipo.

Intanto in Cina, a Shenzhen , si è concluso lo storico trilaterale tra Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin e Xi Jinping . L’incontro è durato circa un’ora e mezza. Prima, si erano svolti i due bilaterali tra il presidente Usa, già in volo per tornare in America, e il capo del Cremlino, e poi con il leader cinese. Verso entrambi Trump ha espresso lodi. Ha elogiato il presidente cinese, definendolo un “leader straordinario”, mentre Xi ha auspicato una cooperazione “aperta e integrata”, mettendo in guardia contro il protezionismo. Incontrando Putin, invece, ha parlato di “un amico” e della volontà comune di porre fine ai conflitti.

Media: “Trump critica gli europei per gli ulteriori miliardi di aiuti a Kiev”

Media: “Trump interviene in collegamento dall'Air Force One al vertice di Berlino”

Kiev: “Putin si atteggia a leader globale, in realtà è un terrorista e criminale”

Meloni via in anticipo dal summit dei Volenterosi, in serata vertice su manovra

Kiev: “Detriti di un drone russo sul ministero degli Esteri”

Media: “Trump ha chiamato gli europei, con Putin è andata bene”

Via telefoni a cronisti Air Force One, ipotesi tappa Pyongyang

Putin: “Abbiamo invitato gli europei a Mosca per comprendere la loro posizione”

Putin: “No ai negoziati sul cessate il fuoco dopo attacco al ponte in Crimea”

Putin in conferenza stampa: “Ucraina ed Europa non sono pronte a compromessi”

Il Cremlino: “L'Ucraina non è stata il tema principale del trilaterale”

Xi a Putin e Trump: “Dobbiamo abbandonare la mentalità da Guerra Fredda”

Trump: “Con Putin lunga discussione sulla guerra, spero voglia la fine”

Trump a Xi e Putin: “Siamo in una posizione unica per discutere di nucleare”

Xi avvisa Trump su Taiwan: “Gli Usa facciano la cosa giusta per evitare una crisi nei rapporti”

Trump: “Usa e Cina vogliono contribuire a porre fine alla guerra in Ucraina”

Xi, Trump e Putin al centro della foto di gruppo a Shenzhen prima del trilaterale

Trump: “È colpa di Obama se Russia e Cina si sono avvicinate”

Il presidente francese, Emmanuel Macron, ha chiesto ai membri della Coalizione dei volenterosi, che si sono visti per la 18esima volta a Berlino, di aiutare l'Ucraina a resistere sul piano militare fino a quando ci saranno veri negoziati. "L'Ucraina resiste sul fronte e riprende terreno, ma la Russia ha deciso di attaccare massicciamente Kiev", ha ricordato nella conferenza stampa seguita all'incontro. "Il primo obbiettivo, se vogliamo essere credibili, è che l'Ucraina tenga e sia nelle migliori condizioni per trattare", ha avvertito, "dunque bisogna fornire sostegno a breve termine a Kiev" e "tutti in questa sala devono fare del loro meglio per inviare subito ciò che possono"

Media: “Trump critica gli europei per gli ulteriori miliardi di aiuti a Kiev”

Il presidente Usa Donald Trump è intervenuto telefonicamente al vertice di Berlino, criticando gli ulteriori miliardi di aiuti all'Ucraina - secondo quanto riportato dai media Politico Germania e Welt. Il tycoon si è collegato al vertice di Berlino dal suo Air Force One per parlare brevemente degli ultimi sviluppi sulla situazione in Ucraina. Durante la telefonata, secondo quanto riferito da due fonti, Trump si sarebbe lasciato andare a uno "sfogo" criticando l'Ue per aver fornito ulteriori miliardi di aiuti all'Ucraina. Secondo un'altra fonte il leader della Casa Bianca avrebbe usato toni più moderati

Merz: “A Shenzhen una photo opportunity, qui a Berlino risultati concrfeti: sostegno a Kiev per tutto il 2027”

"A Shenzhen abbiamo visto photo opportunity. Oggi a Berlino abbiamo ottenuto risultati concreti. Dopo il vertice della Coalizione dei Volenterosi a Berlino possiamo dire in modo ottimista che per tutto l'anno prossimo saremo in grado di sostenere l'Ucraina con forza. Si tratta della nostra sicurezza a tutti. Ieri la Commissione Ue ha presentato una proposta che prevede 45 miliardi aggiuntivi per il 2027 e oggi altri membri della coalizione hanno proposto altri importanti auti come il Regno Unito che ha annunciato altri 11 miliardi di euro di aiuti". Ad affermarlo è il cancelliere tedesco, Friedrich Merz nel corso del suo intervento al termine della riunione della Coalizione dei volenterosi a Berlino sottolineando che anche "i paesi baltici e nordici hanno annunciato misure di sostegno esemplare non per prolungare guerra ma per permettere all'Ucraina di difendersi efficacemente per rendere possibile una negoziazione da un punto di forza"

I partecipanti al vertice della Coalizione dei Volenterosi - che comprende i capi di Stato e di governo di più di 30 Paesi - hanno ricevuto oggi a Berlino dal padrone di casa, il cancelliere tedesco Friedrich Merz, un pezzo del Muro che ha diviso Berlino per 28 anni, dal 1961 al 1989. Il messaggio del Kanzler è che la caduta del Muro ha dimostrato cosa si può ottenere agendo in modo unito e determinato. Un pezzetto di muro è presente anche nella postazione di Merz in conferenza stampa

In conferenza stampa al termine del vertice dei Volenterosi, il cancelliere tedesco Friedrich Merz ha affermato che "il formato di Yalta non porterà la pace" in Ucraina con riferimento al trilaterale di Shenzhen

Il presidente degli Stati Uniti, Donald Trump, ha affermato in un'intervista alla Nbc che non prenderebbe "nessuna decisione finale sulla guerra in Ucraina senza Zelensky". A proposito del vertice di Shenzehen, Trump ha spiegato che l'omologo russo, Vladimir Putin, era "estremamente irritato" per gli attacchi ucraini al Ponte di Crimea" è che ciò è "comprensibile"

Media: “Trump interviene in collegamento dall'Air Force One al vertice di Berlino”

Il presidente americano Donald Trump si è collegato telefonicamente dall'Air Force One al vertice dei Volenterosi sulla guerra in Ucraina in corso a Berlino, dopo l'incontro con il presidente russo Vladimir Putin e il leader cinese Xi Jinping. Secondo quanto riferito da fonti presenti alla riunione, riportano i media tedeschi, Trump ha chiamato sul cellulare il genero Jared Kushner, suo inviato, che ha attivato il vivavoce e amplificato la conversazione con un microfono. A Berlino sono riuniti rappresentanti di 40 Paesi per il più ampio vertice mai organizzato dalla Coalizione dei Volenterosi, con l'obiettivo di ribadire il sostegno all'Ucraina nella difesa contro la Russia

Kiev: “Putin si atteggia a leader globale, in realtà è un terrorista e criminale”

"Putin si è atteggiato a leader globale a Shenzhen. In realtà, è un criminale e terrorista globale. E dovrebbe essere trattato come tale. Esprimiamo la nostra piena solidarietà ai nostri colleghi austriaci e chiediamo una forte risposta internazionale agli attacchi brutali della Russia". Lo afferma su X il ministro degli Esteri ucraino Andrii Sybiha, dopo i raid con droni russi vicino all'ambasciata d'Austria e a quella di Paesi Bassi a Kiev. Attacchi che hanno provocato almeno un morto

La ministra degli Esteri austriaca Beate Meinl-Reisinger ha reso noto che anche l'ambasciata austriaca a Kiev è stata danneggiata durante gli attacchi con droni che hanno colpito oggi la città. "Questo pomeriggio, un proiettile ha colpito proprio davanti alla nostra ambasciata austriaca nel centro di Kiev. L'edificio è stato danneggiato. Fortunatamente, nessuno è rimasto ferito!", ha dichiarato, scrive il Guardian. "Alla luce dei crescenti e intensi attacchi russi contro Kiev, ho pertanto disposto ulteriori misure per proteggere ulteriormente il nostro personale - ha aggiunto -. Un ringraziamento speciale va a tutto il team dell'ambasciata, che lavora quotidianamente per l'Austria in queste condizioni difficili e pericolose. Nutriamo il massimo rispetto per la vostra dedizione". Poco prima era giunta notizia dell'attacco vicino ad un'altra sede diplomatica: quella olandese. Un drone russo si è schiantato vicino all'ambasciata dei Paesi Bassi nella capitale ucraina, danneggiando alcune auto, un posto di guardia e mandando in frantumi i vetri dell'edificio

Meloni via in anticipo dal summit dei Volenterosi, in serata vertice su manovra

La presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni, a quanto si apprende, lascerà con un'ora di anticipo i lavori del vertice della Coalizione dei Volenterosi, ancora in corso a Berlino, per poter partecipare in serata a un vertice di maggioranza sulla manovra, previsto in videoconferenza

Kiev: “Detriti di un drone russo sul ministero degli Esteri”

Resti di uno dei droni lanciati oggi pomeriggio dalla Russia su Kiev sono stati ritrovati nei pressi del ministero degli Affari Esteri ucraino. Lo annuncia il ministro degli Esteri ucraino Andriy Sybiha, aggiungendo, come riportano i media ucraini, che "i diplomatici aggiungeranno i detriti al loro museo"

Media: “Trump ha chiamato gli europei, con Putin è andata bene”

Donald Trump ha chiamato i leader europei radunati a Berlino dall'Air Force One e ha riferito loro che il suo colloquio con Vladimir Putin è andato bene e contribuirà a favorire la pace in Ucraina. Lo riporta l'agenzia Bloomberg citando alcune fonti. A Berlino è riunita la “coalizione dei volenterosi”

items.content:
Mercoledì Katie Koenig, una portavoce della flotta statunitense del Pacifico, ha detto che una delle tre portaerei che gli Stati Uniti avevano inviato in Medio Oriente, la USS George Washington, ha lasciato l’area ed è stata destinata a nuove operazioni nella regione dell’Asia e del Pacifico.
